close_reason: Added <Object>Filter aliases to 6 sibling extension-types crates (calendars: CalendarFilter, CalendarEventFilter, NotificationFilter; tasks: TaskFilter, TaskNotificationFilter; contacts: ContactCardFilter; filenode: FileNodeFilter; sharing: PrincipalFilter, ShareNotificationFilter; metadata: MetadataFilter). Re-exported jmap_types::query::{Filter, FilterOperator, Operator} at each crate's lib.rs root. Also filled in MailboxFilter on mail-types canonical (was missing from EmailFilter/EmailSubmissionFilter pair). Non-breaking pure additions. Workspace cargo check + clippy + test + rustdoc on changed type crates all clean. Commit 559edc1.
description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:14-23 (canonical: re-exports plus the typed aliases)

The mail-canonical-template crate provides three things at its `query` module top:

    pub use jmap_types::query::{Filter, FilterOperator, Operator};
    pub type EmailFilter = Filter<EmailFilterCondition>;
    pub type EmailSubmissionFilter = Filter<EmailSubmissionFilterCondition>;

This lets callers write `jmap_mail_types::EmailFilter::Condition(...)` without ever having to import `jmap_types`.

**Divergence**: every other extension types crate that defines a `FilterCondition` does NOT provide the analogous re-exports or aliases:

| Crate | `FilterCondition` defined | Re-exports `Filter`/`FilterOperator`/`Operator` from jmap-types? | `<Object>Filter` alias? |
|---|---|---|---|
| jmap-mail-types | ✓ Email, Mailbox, EmailSubmission | ✓ | ✓ EmailFilter, EmailSubmissionFilter |
| jmap-calendars-types | ✓ Calendar, CalendarEvent, Notification | ✗ | ✗ (no `CalendarFilter`, `CalendarEventFilter`, `NotificationFilter` aliases) |
| jmap-tasks-types | ✓ Task, TaskNotification | ✗ | ✗ |
| jmap-contacts-types | ✓ ContactCard | ✗ | ✗ |
| jmap-filenode-types | ✓ FileNode | ✗ | ✗ |
| jmap-sharing-types | ✓ Principal, ShareNotification | ✗ | ✗ |
| jmap-metadata-types | ✓ Metadata | ✗ | ✗ |
| jmap-chat-types | ✗ (separate bead JMAP-ops7.7) | ✗ | ✗ |

**What goes wrong**:

1. A consumer of `jmap-tasks-types` who wants to write a typed filter expression must write:

       use jmap_tasks_types::TaskFilterCondition;
       use jmap_types::Filter;               // <-- second crate import
       let f: Filter<TaskFilterCondition> = Filter::Condition(TaskFilterCondition::HasKeyword("flagged".into()));

   With the alias they would write:

       use jmap_tasks_types::{TaskFilter, TaskFilterCondition};
       let f: TaskFilter = TaskFilter::Condition(TaskFilterCondition::HasKeyword("flagged".into()));

   Same number of bytes, but the consumer never has to know `jmap-types` exists, which is the cookie-cutter property the workspace AGENTS.md README convention claims for sibling type crates.

2. Workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" section names `jmap-mail-types` as the canonical extension-types template that all 7 siblings should mirror. The aliases at mail-types/src/query.rs:14-23 are part of that canonical shape. The 6 siblings without them are silent template divergences.

3. A future extension types crate added to the workspace will read `jmap-mail-types` as the canonical and mirror the alias pattern, then find inconsistent prior art in the 6 siblings without it. The convention is ambiguous as-is.

**Fix**: in each of calendars-types, tasks-types, contacts-types, filenode-types, sharing-types, metadata-types, add the canonical 3-line block plus per-`FilterCondition` alias:

    pub use jmap_types::query::{Filter, FilterOperator, Operator};
    pub type CalendarFilter = Filter<CalendarFilterCondition>;
    pub type CalendarEventFilter = Filter<CalendarEventFilterCondition>;
    pub type NotificationFilter = Filter<NotificationFilterCondition>;   // (and so on)

Non-breaking: pure addition. Sibling type-crate users gain a shorter, cookie-cutter-consistent shape; existing callers reaching into `jmap_types::` directly continue to work.

Per the workspace canonical-template propagation rule, this is a "propagate canonical to siblings" sweep, not a "change canonical and follow up".
title: 6 of 8 extension types crates lack the canonical `<Object>Filter = Filter<XxxFilterCondition>` aliases that mail-types exports; callers must reach into `jmap_types::Filter` directly
